questions.question: What makes Janusz start researching the Black Code?
answers: He finds a family diary from Haiti
He reads that the document formally remained in force until 28 May 2026
He gets a grant to study Polish law
He hears about it in a church in Kraków
questions.explanation: The trigger is the information about the surprisingly late repeal of the document.

questions.question: What function does Vodou serve in Jean-Pierre's interpretation?
answers: Only an exotic religion from the movies
A tool of survival, order and resistance
A private cult of a few families
A religion imported from Poland
questions.explanation: Jean-Pierre presents Vodou as a social system and a tool of survival.

questions.question: Why is Bois Caïman important in the story?
answers: It's the birthplace of Polish emigration
It's the site of the ritual that preceded the Haitian revolution
It's the former seat of Napoleon
It's a museum of colonial law
questions.explanation: Jean-Pierre describes Bois Caïman as the site of the ritual connected with the start of the uprising.

questions.question: How does the text interpret the link between Our Lady of Częstochowa and Erzulie Dantor?
answers: As a historical translation error
As an example of religious syncretism and survival
As proof of Vatican dominance
As a modern marketing campaign
questions.explanation: The thread serves to show how religious symbols were absorbed and transformed.

questions.question: What broader lesson does Janusz take from the journey?
answers: That the history of slavery belongs only to the past
That the spirit of the Black Code lives on in prejudices and in the treatment of 'others'
That Vodou can only be explained by magic
That Poland and Haiti have no points of contact
questions.explanation: At the end Janusz writes about the persistence of the law's spirit in today's prejudices.
